nodes.label: Thin OpenAI-Compatible LLM Client
nodes.rationale: The wire format is the commodity: Groq, OpenRouter, Gemini's compatibility endpoint, Together, Ollama and OpenAI all speak the same /chat/completions shape, so one ~50-line client covers every provider without a per-vendor code branch. A vendor SDK would buy typed errors at the cost of pinning the project to one vendor's release cadence. AI_LLM_BASE_URL + AI_LLM_MODEL + AI_LLM_API_KEY select the provider; the only new dependency is httpx==0.28.1.

nodes.label: LiveLLMClient
nodes.rationale: Maps LiveCandidatePayload objects into DiagnosisCandidate and resolves symptom names into trend refs. Touches no Session and imports no repository, so the pipeline remains unit-testable without a database. Exceptions are not caught inside it because the orchestrator already maps provider exceptions to the correct AIError codes.

nodes.label: LiveCandidatePayload (narrow intermediate schema)
nodes.rationale: Handing a model DiagnosisCandidate.model_json_schema() would be actively harmful: the likelihood_band computed field appears in the serialization schema, a model shown that schema will echo it back, and extra="forbid" then rejects the response, turning deliberate strictness into a self-inflicted failure on every call. The payload carries only what a model should author: evidence_document_ids (ids selected from the supplied list) and trend_symptom_names (names, never UUIDs).

nodes.label: Hard/Soft Failure Line for Model Output
nodes.rationale: Structural violations fail hard; per-candidate content violations are normalized or dropped. A malformed envelope means the provider is broken, while one over-confident or uncited candidate among five means the model was imprecise about one row. Raising on the latter destroys an otherwise-good analysis and, because every failure precedes the first write, costs the clinician the whole run. Dropping is not lenient: a dropped candidate never reaches the database and an unresolved citation is discarded rather than persisted.

nodes.label: category Is Derived, Not Accepted
nodes.rationale: Corrected after the first live call: honouring the model's category made openai/gpt-oss-120b return Parkinson's disease at confidence 0.78 flagged early_watch, which contradicts ADR-003 decision 4 and meant early_watch denoted a low-confidence watch under the mock and any trend-backed finding under a live model. Because category is rendered by the UI and the PDF, which cannot tell which provider produced it, a field whose meaning varies by provider defeats the seam more quietly than one whose type does.

nodes.label: System-Authored trend_basis UUIDs
nodes.rationale: A model that authors UUIDs breaks the premise that a dangling reference means staleness rather than corruption: a fabricated id would be indistinguishable from a stale one and the traceability chain would silently become unfalsifiable. The model names worsening symptoms; the client resolves those names through normalize_symptom_name against context.trends and builds refs from real TrendPoint rows. Same principle as _resolve_evidence: a provider selects, the system resolves.

nodes.label: trends.trend_basis_refs() Shared Builder
nodes.rationale: Extracted to app/ai/trends and used by both the mock and live providers so there is one implementation rather than two. trends.py gains an import from app.schemas.analysis for TrendBasisRef with no cycle.

nodes.label: HYBRID_PIPELINE_NOTE
nodes.rationale: With a live LLM and a mocked retriever, the old expression would stamp 'evidence retrieved from live corpus' onto an analysis whose evidence came from mock_corpus.py, disabling the one technical mitigation on record at the exact moment it starts mattering. Selection now reads retriever.provenance alongside reasoning.provider_mode. ADR-003's prediction about not touching the orchestrator is knowingly broken because honest labelling outranks a prediction about file scope.

nodes.label: provider_mode Is Not Widened to hybrid
nodes.rationale: It is persisted on analyses.provider_mode and exposed on AnalysisResponse, so a third member means a migration, a wire-contract change for the frontend and REPORT-01, and a new state every consumer must learn. pipeline_note is already a free-text field carried on every analysis for exactly this purpose.

nodes.label: AI_PROVIDER Defaults to mock
nodes.rationale: Live reasoning is opt-in per environment, and build_providers() raises a configuration error if live-llm is selected without an API key so the failure lands at startup rather than mid-request on a clinician's screen. The mock provider is not deprecated: it keeps the test suite network-free and deterministic. The only irreversible artifact of going live is external, since prompts already sent to a third party cannot be recalled.

nodes.label: Clinical Context Leaves the Machine
nodes.rationale: A live call sends visit history, symptoms and clinician free text to a third-party API, acceptable only under the unconfirmed synthetic-demo-data assumption. Free tiers may retain or train on submitted data. Pointing live-llm at real patient data requires a security review and is not authorized by this ADR. No prompt or response body may be logged; logging is restricted to model name, latency, HTTP status, visit_id and candidate count.

nodes.label: Prompt-Injection Surface
nodes.rationale: Clinician free text (chief_complaint, history, notes, observation) now reaches a model prompt. Structural mitigations already in place for other reasons contain it: schema validation at the seam, evidence re-resolution, system-authored UUIDs, so the worst realistic outcome is a degraded or dropped candidate. This gets materially worse when real retrieval lands, because a corpus document is a far more attractive injection vector than a symptom field.

nodes.label: Determinism Lost on the Live Path
nodes.rationale: No equivalent to the mock's byte-identical-JSON guarantee exists or can exist for a live model; get_latest_for_visit ordering by created_at DESC already accommodates re-runs producing different candidates.

nodes.label: Test Suite Pinned to the Mock Provider
nodes.rationale: Several suites call build_providers() with no argument, reading the real Settings; with a second AI_PROVIDER value a developer whose backend/.env selected live-llm had the suite issue real model calls, observed as ten tests hitting Groq and tripling run time. tests/conftest.py now sets AI_PROVIDER=mock in the environment, which outranks the .env file; live-provider tests build their own Settings and drive an httpx.MockTransport.

nodes.label: Hosted Model Id Is Not a Stable Identifier
nodes.rationale: The first configured default, llama-3.3-70b-versatile, was already retired at first live call and returned 404 model_not_found; the default is now openai/gpt-oss-120b. A model id in configuration is a dependency that can be retired without a release on our side.

edges.source_location: Context — 'ADR-003 built the seam for exactly this'
Why — 'the same principle as _resolve_evidence, applied to the other half of the traceability chain'
Decision 3 vs ADR-001 Decision — both make the caller-visible signal uniform and push the distinguishing detail into server-side handling
Decision 1 — httpx==0.28.1 promoted into requirements.txt, extending the documented stack
